Traditional restrictive diets can help you lose weight in short bursts (aka the “yo-yo” effect), but ultimately don’t help you keep the weight off.

Noom can help you create long-term results through habit and behavior change, not restrictive dieting.

Going back to the concept of caloric density, all the foods previously shown are considered medium caloric density. Noom calls these “yellow foods”.

CALORIC
DENSITY
=
CALORIES

Studies have proven that caloric density (not calories) determines how full you feel. And how full you feel dictates how you eat, and how you lose weight.

We’ll help you closely measure caloric density to stay full on less calories!

There's room for those and more with Noom!

We label them “orange foods” for simplicity, but none of these foods are "bad foods". They do have higher caloric density though, meaning they’ll keep you less full.

As a result, we need to be mindful about how much orange we’re eating. But we don’t need to cut them out altogether - giving up treats forever is neither sustainable nor yummy!

Noom's Food Philosophy is simple: eat more food with a low caloric density.

While it's ideal to eat “green foods”, we know it's hard to just eat leaves (we're not rabbits). Noom will help you find balance to eat the foods you love and still lose weight!

You’re right!

Grapes are the smarter snack. But wait, aren’t raisins just dried grapes?

Well that’s exactly it. Juicy grapes are 81% water. And because of that, it’ll help you feel full faster.

This life hack is explained by the principles of caloric density. We’ll teach you more about that soon, including how you can use it to eat healthier without cutting out all your favorite foods.

How can mindful eating help you?
Lose more weight
Increase your self-awareness
Both

screens.title: Noom: Stop dieting. Get lifelong results.
screens.visibleText:
PESQUISA
P

Best Answer: Both

Mindful eating is the practice of eating with Intention and Attention.

Intention means actively deciding what you're eating (and not just reaching for the food that's in front of you).
Attention means focusing on the meal while you eat (not distracted by today's to-do list).

Mindful eating slows you down and increases your self-awareness. This way you eat fewer calories and make healthier food choices!

Next

First thing after you wake - before you've consumed anything
Once you've eaten your last meal of the day

You’re right!

Weight can fluctuate daily based on the food we eat. It's best to weigh yourself at the same time, on the same scale, every day on an empty stomach.

The International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity reported that frequent self-weighing can lead to weight loss and better weight maintenance. A daily weigh-in schedule creates self-awareness & helps you make healthy choices!
